perceptual_contract.primary_success_condition: A coupled spatial control states the broad source-relative visible result first, then retains every material member relation that the summary only partially carries or loses, without duplicating ownership or forcing detail when the summary is sufficient.
perceptual_contract.user_appeal: Keep the source's non-neutral pose and viewing relation from collapsing into a generic centered frontal result while preserving a coherent large-scale direction.

invariants.statement: Every invariant coupled effect has one source-relative macro summary that appears first inside its single aggregate control.
Every coupled member is assessed exactly once, and each source-visible result classified partial or lost remains a literal residual subclause in the same coupled control.
A sufficient summary emits no member residuals, and complete or not-applicable members remain non-emitted so detail cannot become a universal pose preset or duplicate salience.
Runtime rules contain no preferred centering, frontality, side, angle, body part, cue count, subject class, phrase, coordinate, or generator-specific workaround.

flexible_dimensions: actual source direction and mirrored orientation
whether a coupled summary is sufficient, lossy, or uncertain
which and how many member relations remain at risk
literal source-supported wording and stochastic rendered pixels

mismatches.source_state: Several weak source-visible relations may jointly establish one macro direction while still carrying distinct residual information.
mismatches.render_state: The v3 aggregate-control rule proved one owner and one macro result but did not prove which member relations its compact summary preserved or erased.

mismatches.source_state: Material residual relations need literal actuation when a summary is lossy, but complete member results need no extra wording.
mismatches.render_state: The previous binary choice between one summary and separate member controls could either omit source detail or duplicate and over-amplify it.

hypotheses.statement: A coupled label or macro result is a lossy summary unless its coverage of every source-visible member result is explicitly assessed.
hypotheses.falsifier: Unrelated coupled-orientation cases retain all material member relations from a summary-only control without per-member coverage or residual actuation.

hypotheses.statement: Putting one macro summary first and only at-risk residuals immediately after it preserves global direction while avoiding both detail loss and duplicate control ownership.
hypotheses.falsifier: Held-out prompt or render comparisons show that the hierarchy systematically weakens macro direction, duplicates salience, or performs worse than summary-only and fully decomposed controls.

intervention.general_rule: Use spatial-orientation/v4. An invariant coupled effect keeps one relation/effect/claim/control path; inside that control, write a source-relative summary anchor first, classify its adequacy, cover every member exactly once, and append literal residual subclauses only for partial or lost member results.
intervention.generalization_basis: The rule operates on source-owned member ids, visible results, evidence, adequacy, and containment rather than any target direction or named pose. Sufficient, lossy, uncertain, partial, human, and non-human fixtures exercise opposite detail budgets without selecting a preferred output.

decision.rationale: The candidate now rejects the exact v3 summary-only coupled plan and passes source-neutral fixtures for sufficient, lossy, uncertain, partial, duplicate, ordering, and non-human behavior. No independent post-change prompt generation or image render was performed in this apply-only turn, so pixel fidelity and post-change user preference remain unscored and the intervention is not promoted beyond structural implementation.
